research_question: What is the effect of treatment of acute malnutrition (wasting) in children aged 6 to 59 months delivered by lay health workers compared with health professionals in health facilities on recovery from wasting?
outcome_description: Proportion of children aged 6 to 59 months who recovered or were discharged cured from acute malnutrition/wasting at the end of treatment (using trial's own definition of recovery/cure).
positive_direction: Higher recovery or cure rate among children treated by lay health workers compared with health professionals (RR > 1).
search_queries: community health workers acute malnutrition wasting treatment trial
lay health worker severe acute malnutrition recovery controlled trial
community management acute malnutrition health facility comparison
inclusion_criteria: Children aged 6 to 59 months with acute malnutrition (wasting, including severe or moderate acute malnutrition).

Empirical comparative studies (randomised controlled trials, cluster-randomised trials, or non-randomised comparative studies) comparing treatment delivered by lay/community health workers versus health professionals in facilities.
Reports quantitative data on recovery or cure at the end of treatment.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, or study protocols).
No comparison between lay health worker delivery and facility-based health professional delivery (e.g. both arms delivered by lay workers, or single-arm intervention studies).
No quantitative data on recovery or cure rates from acute malnutrition that allow computation of an effect size.
Studies conducted exclusively in adult populations or evaluating solely prevention of malnutrition rather than treatment of existing wasting.
moderators_to_extract: Severity of acute malnutrition (SAM vs MAM vs combined)
Study design (individual RCT vs cluster RCT vs non-randomised controlled study)
Cadre of lay provider (paid community health worker vs unpaid volunteer)
Cluster adjustment status (adjusted in primary study vs unadjusted with ICC correction)
effect_size_note: Risk ratio (RR) of recovery calculated as the risk of cure/recovery in the lay health worker arm divided by the risk in the health professional arm. For cluster-randomised trials without reported cluster adjustment, standard errors of log RR are inflated using design effect 1 + (m - 1) * ICC with assumed ICC = 0.02 (sensitivity analysis at 0.05). Arms oriented such that RR > 1 indicates higher recovery with lay health workers.
